book.title: The Summer I Learned to Swim
book.author: Jun Hartley

lines: Everyone in my family could swim except me.
My cousins launched themselves off the dock like cannonballs with opinions.
My dad could float for an hour, hands folded behind his head, like a man resting on an invisible couch.
I stood at the edge in my too-big goggles and negotiated with the lake.
That summer, the new girl next door, Mai, offered to teach me, and I said yes before my fear could speak.
She did not tell me it was easy.
"It's not about being brave," she said.
"It's about letting the water hold you.
It's very, very rude of you not to trust it."
The first time my feet left the bottom, I screamed.
By August I could cross the shallow end, and on the last night of the holidays I was floating on my back, ears under, listening to the lake hum like a refrigerator the size of the world.
I could see Mai's shape on the dock against the first stars.
For one second I understood that being held by something does not mean you have stopped being yourself.
